mainTopic: Damages for a pregnant woman (heirs, ex-husband, and דמי ולדות), then whether כופר and the thirty shekels depend on the ox being stoned
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: when a pregnant woman is struck and has no heirs, the attacker keeps the money. The ברייתא implies her own payments go to her heirs and not to her husband. רבה and רב נחמן explain that she was a גרושה. The גמרא asks why a גרושה would not share in the דמי ולדות, and רב פפא answers from the פסוק 'בעל האשה' that this payment always belongs to the child's father. The גמרא then asks why רבה and רב נחמן did not use their own money-versus-land rule from the case of a בכור. It answers that this rule follows the רבנן, while here they follow רבי. A new topic follows: ריש לקיש and רבה rule that if an ox kills unintentionally, there are no thirty shekels for a slave and no כופר for a free person, because these payments depend on the ox being stoned. אביי challenges רבה from a משנה about a man who admits his ox killed someone. The משנה is first explained as speaking of ordinary damages. אביי pushes back from the last part of that משנה, and רבה insists both parts are about damages, with his explanation continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: no heirs, so the attacker keeps the money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list: if the woman was a freed שפחה or a גיורת with no heirs, the attacker 'wins' and pays nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא the גמרא quoted at the end of the previous daf. It says that when there are no heirs, the attacker keeps the money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumes the woman's own payments go to her heirs, not to her husband. That is a problem, because a husband normally inherits his wife. This tension is what the next steps try to resolve.

keyTerms.meaning: A female convert, who has no Jewish relatives to inherit her
He gains: the attacker keeps the money since no one can collect

phrases.english: or a convert: he gains!
phrases.notes: This finishes the ברייתא from the last daf. 'He' is the attacker: he pays no one, since there are no heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous daf, which is being used to raise a difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a husband inherits his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sends the woman's payments to her heirs, not her husband. That clashes with the husband's normal right to inherit her.

steps.title: רבה and רב נחמן: the case is a divorcée
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב נחמן both explain that the ברייתא speaks of a גרושה, so the ex-husband does not inherit her.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is about a divorcée. And רב נחמן also said: It is about a divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the problem the same way: the woman in the ברייתא is divorced.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once they are divorced, he is no longer her husband and does not inherit her. So her payments naturally go to her heirs. That fits the wording of the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A divorced woman
And likewise said: a second sage said the same thing

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is about a divorcée.
And likewise Rav Nachman said: It is about a divorcée.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty from the ברייתא by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to speak of a married woman, which would contradict the husband's inheritance.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of a גרושה, whom the ex-husband does not inherit.

steps.title: Challenge: then the divorcée should share in the payment for the offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if she is divorced, why does the ex-husband get all the דמי ולדות? She should get a share.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: If she is a divorcée, she should also share in the payment for the offspring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of רבה and רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives all the דמי ולדות to the husband. If the couple is divorced, why should he get it all? She should take part of it.

keyTerms.meaning: She should split, take a share
Payment for the lost offspring (the miscarried fetus)

phrases.english: They said: a divorcée, then, also
should share in the payment for the offspring!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: גְּרוּשָׁה נָמֵי תִּיפְלוֹג בִּדְמֵי וְלָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer that the ברייתא speaks of a גרושה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of רבה and רב נחמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he is no longer her husband, she should get a share of the דמי ולדות, yet the ברייתא gives it all to him.

steps.title: רב פפא: the Torah gives the offspring payment to the father, even without marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the Torah gives דמי ולדות to the man who fathered the child, even through זנות, based on 'בעל האשה'. So a divorced ex-husband still collects it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The Torah gave the payment for the offspring to the husband, even if he was with her through licentious relations. What is the reason? The verse says: 'As the husband of the woman shall impose upon him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge and proves his point from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בעל here does not mean 'legal husband'. It means the man who was with her and fathered the child. So the payment goes to him whether they are married, divorced, or never married at all, and divorce does not shift any of it to her.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, awarded ownership
Through licentious relations, outside of marriage
'The husband of the woman': read as the man who was with her

steps.whatToRemember: דמי ולדות belong to the child's father because the Torah calls him בעל האשה, even if he was never her legal husband. So the ברייתא can speak of a גרושה, and the ex-husband still collects all of it.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'בעל' here as 'legal husband'. רב פפא reads it as 'the man who was with her', which is why marriage does not matter.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The Torah awarded the payment for the offspring to the husband,
even if he was with her through licentious relations.
What is the reason? The verse says:
'As the husband of the woman shall impose upon him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַתּוֹרָה זִכְּתָה דְּמֵי וְלָדוֹת לַבַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that a גרושה should share in the דמי ולדות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק to define who owns the payment
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The payment seemed tied to the marriage, so a divorcée should get part of it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The payment belongs to the father of the child (בעל = the man who was with her), whether or not they are married.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule that the right to דמי ולדות comes from fathering the child, not from being married. That is why the explanation of the ברייתא as a גרושה can stand.

steps.title: Why not use their own money-versus-land rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה and רב נחמן: instead of saying the woman was a גרושה, each could have explained the ברייתא using his own opinion about collected money and collected land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us explain the ברייתא, according to רבה, as a case where they collected money, and according to רב נחמן, as a case where they collected land! For רבה said: if they collected land, the בכור has a double portion; if they collected money, he does not. And רב נחמן said: if they collected money, he has a double portion; if they collected land, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבה and רב נחמן needed the גרושה answer at all. Each of them already has a rule that could explain why the husband does not inherit, so the גרושה answer seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור gets a double portion only of what his father already owned (מוחזק), not of what was only owed to him (ראוי). רבה and רב נחמן each say one type of collection counts as only 'owed.' In the same way, a husband inherits only what his wife already owned, so each רב could have said the payment was only 'owed' to her and the husband does not get it, even if she was still married.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us establish it (explain the case as)
They collected (a debt or payment)
Money, coins
Land
Firstborn son, who gets a double share of his father's estate
Property only owed versus property already owned

steps.confusionAlert: רבה and רב נחמן say opposite things here. Do not mix them up: for רבה, land counts as already owned; for רב נחמן, money counts as already owned.

phrases.english: Let us establish it, according to Rabba,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא about the woman with no heirs, where the attacker pays nothing.

phrases.english: as a case where they collected money,
and according to Rav Nachman, as a case where they collected land!
For Rabba said:
If they collected land, he has a double portion,
if they collected money, he does not have one.
And Rav Nachman said:
If they collected money, he has a double portion,
if they collected land, he does not have one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the גרושה answer from step 2 and asks why it was needed at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of רבה and רב נחמן that the ברייתא speaks of a גרושה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each רב has his own rule that would make the payment count as only 'owed' (ראוי), which a husband does not inherit. So the ברייתא could be about a married woman, and the גרושה answer is not needed.

steps.title: Their money-versus-land rule follows the רבנן, but here they follow רבי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the money-versus-land opinions were said only to explain the רבנן as taught in ארץ ישראל. Here רבה and רב נחמן follow רבי, so they had to say the woman was a גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement was said according to the scholars of the West, following the רבנן. When רבה and רב נחמן speak here, they follow רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the money-versus-land rule does not apply here. That rule was said only according to one opinion, and here רבה and רב נחמן follow a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן limit what counts as the father's property, so for them it matters whether money or land was collected. רבי holds that a בכור gets a double share even of growth in value after the father's death, so everything owed counts as already owned. Following רבי, a husband would inherit the payment, so the only way he loses it is if she was a גרושה.

keyTerms.meaning: That statement / that rule applies only to...
People of the West, meaning the scholars of ארץ ישראל
According to the opinion of the רבנן
Growth in value of property

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי, everything owed counts as already owned, so the husband would inherit. That is why רבה and רב נחמן had to explain the ברייתא as speaking of a גרושה, and why her ex-husband gets nothing from the payments for her own injury. He still collects the דמי ולדות, as רב פפא explained in step 4.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one answer can depend on which תנא's view you follow. A rule a אמורא gives in one place may only be explaining one side of a מחלוקת, not his own final view.

phrases.english: That statement is according to the people of the West,
phrases.notes: 'That statement' is the money-versus-land rule of רבה and רב נחמן from the last step.

phrases.english: following the opinion of the Rabbis;
when they speak here, it is according to Rebbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לִבְנֵי מַעְרְבָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 by limiting the money-versus-land rule to the opinion of the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinions: the rule from the case of the בכור follows the רבנן, while this sugya follows רבי.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבה and רב נחמן could use their money-versus-land rule to explain the ברייתא even for a married woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here they follow רבי, for whom everything owed counts as already owned, so a husband would inherit. The ברייתא must therefore be about a גרושה.

steps.title: No thirty shekels when an ox kills a slave by accident
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש rules that an owner whose ox killed an עבד unintentionally is exempt from the thirty shekels, because the פסוק ties the payment to the ox being stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש says: if an ox killed a slave without meaning to, the owner does not pay thirty shekels. The פסוק says 'thirty shekels of silver he shall give to his master, and the ox shall be stoned.' This teaches that the owner pays thirty shekels only when the ox is stoned. If the ox is not stoned, the owner does not pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a rule from ריש לקיש about an ox that killed an עבד by accident.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places the thirty shekels and the stoning of the ox side by side. ריש לקיש reads this as a link: no stoning means no thirty shekels. An ox that kills unintentionally is not stoned, so the owner is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Unintentionally, without meaning to
The fixed thirty-shekel payment for an ox that kills a slave
Stoning, the death penalty for an ox that kills a person
A non-Jewish slave

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says:
An ox that killed the slave
unintentionally
the owner is exempt from the thirty shekels,
as it is stated:
"Thirty shekels of silver he shall give to his master,
and the ox shall be stoned"
Whenever the ox is subject to stoning,
the owners pay thirty shekels;
when the ox is not subject to stoning,
the owners do not pay thirty shekels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of רבה and רב נחמן ended in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that killed an עבד unintentionally: the owner is exempt from the thirty shekels, because that payment depends on the ox being stoned.

steps.title: No כופר when an ox kills a free person by accident
steps.stepSummary: רבה applies the same reasoning to כופר: if an ox killed a free person unintentionally, the owner does not pay כופר, because the פסוק ties כופר to the ox being stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה says: if an ox killed a free person without meaning to, the owner does not pay כופר. The פסוק says 'the ox shall be stoned, and its owner also shall be put to death. If a כופר is placed on him.' This teaches that the owner pays כופר only when the ox is stoned. If the ox is not stoned, the owner does not pay כופר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a rule parallel to ריש לקיש's, this time about כופר for killing a free person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions stoning the ox right before it mentions כופר. רבה learns from this that כופר depends on stoning. An ox that kills by accident is not stoned, so there is no כופר.

keyTerms.meaning: A free person, not a slave
Ransom money the owner pays when his ox kills a person
Is placed upon him

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule makes כופר fully dependent on the ox being stoned. That is exactly the point אביי will attack next.

phrases.english: Rabba says:
An ox that killed a free person
unintentionally
the owner is exempt from ransom,
as it is stated: "The ox shall be stoned,
and its owner also shall be put to death.
If a ransom is placed on him"
Whenever the ox is subject to stoning,
the owners pay ransom;
when the ox is not subject to stoning,
the owners do not pay ransom.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same kind of reasoning as ריש לקיש in step 7, this time to כופר for a free person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that killed a free person unintentionally: the owner is exempt from כופר, because כופר depends on the ox being stoned.

steps.title: אביי challenges רבה from a man who admits his ox killed someone
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a משנה: a man who says 'my ox killed so-and-so' pays based on his own admission. The ox cannot be stoned on its owner's word alone, so if this payment is כופר, then כופר does not depend on stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי challenged רבה: we learned that if someone says 'my ox killed so-and-so' or 'my ox killed so-and-so's ox,' he pays based on his own word. What is he paying? Isn't it כופר?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's rule with a case where it seems כופר is paid even though the ox is not stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ox is never stoned because of what its owner says, so here there is no stoning. Yet the owner pays. This payment cannot be a קנס (a fine), because a fine is not paid on one's own admission. So אביי suggests it must be כופר, and that would mean כופר is paid without stoning, against רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so, some person
Based on his own admission
What, is it not...? A way of proposing how to read a source

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not arguing about 'unintentionally.' He is attacking רבה's basic idea that כופר is paid only when the ox is stoned.

phrases.english: Abaye raised an objection to him:
"My ox killed so-and-so,"
phrases.notes: אביי is quoting a משנה here.

phrases.english: or "my ox killed the ox of so-and-so"

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם עַל פִּי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: this man pays based on his own word.
What is this payment? Is it not ransom?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that כופר is paid only when the ox is stoned.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who admits his ox killed a person pays on his own word, even though the ox is not stoned on that word. If the payment is כופר, then כופר does not depend on stoning.

steps.title: The payment is ordinary damages, not כופר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means דמים, ordinary money damages, not כופר. So רבה's rule still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the payment is the money value of the damage, not כופר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבה by reading the משנה as talking about regular damages rather than כופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner who admits his ox killed someone does pay something, but that payment is ordinary damages. He does not pay כופר, because the ox is not stoned. So the משנה does not contradict רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Money value, ordinary damages

steps.whatToRemember: רבה holds that כופר is paid only when the ox is stoned. The case of a man who admits his ox killed someone is explained as ordinary damages (דמים), not כופר.

phrases.english: No, it means the money value.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting which payment the source is talking about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The payment made on one's own admission is כופר, which would show that כופר does not depend on stoning.
steps.terutzMaskana: The payment is דמים, ordinary damages. כופר still depends on stoning, as רבה said.

steps.title: אביי challenges the 'damages' answer from the last part of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that if the משנה is about דמים, its last part makes no sense. A man who admits his ox killed a slave would have to pay, yet the משנה says he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה means money damages, look at its last part: 'My ox killed so-and-so's slave.' There the owner does not pay based on his own word. But if the משנה is about money damages, why shouldn't he pay?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the answer from Step 10 by quoting the last part of the same משנה, which is about a slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who admits he owes ordinary damages must pay, but a person who admits to a קנס (a fine) is exempt. The משנה says the owner who admits his ox killed a slave does not pay, so that payment looks like the thirty-shekel קנס, not damages. This suggests the whole משנה is about fixed Torah payments, and the first part would then be כופר after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Money damages: the actual value of what was lost
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
Based on his own word or admission

phrases.english: If it is money damages, say the last part:
"My ox killed so-and-so's slave"
he does not pay based on his own word.
And if it is money damages, why not?
phrases.notes: Someone who admits he owes damages pays. Only a fine falls away when it is based on the person's own admission.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 10 that the משנה refers to דמים
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 10 that the משנה's payment is דמים, not כופר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last part of the משנה exempts someone who admits to his ox killing a slave. That only makes sense for a קנס, since damages are paid even on admission. So the משנה seems to deal with Torah-fixed payments, which would make the first part כופר and contradict רבה.

steps.title: רבה refuses a forced split and says both parts are about damages
steps.stepSummary: רבה says he could answer that the first part is damages and the last part is a קנס, but that would be a forced answer. Instead he holds that both parts are about דמים, and the גמרא goes on to explain how.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to אביי: I could answer you that the first part is about damages and the last part is about a fine. But I will not give you a forced answer. Both this part and that part are about damages.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's challenge. He sets aside an easy but forced answer and states that both parts of the משנה are about damages. This sets up the next lines, which explain why the owner does not pay damages for the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The easy way out would be to say the משנה switches topics midway, from damages in the first part to the קנס of thirty shekels in the last part. רבה rejects this because it is strained to read one משנה as talking about two different kinds of payment. He keeps the משנה consistent: both parts are about damages, so he still needs to explain the exemption in the last part.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a משנה or ברייתא
A fine: a fixed Torah payment that is not based on the actual loss
A forced, strained answer
Both this one and that one

steps.confusionAlert: רבה does not accept the 'first part damages, last part fine' answer. He only mentions it in order to reject it. His real position is that both parts are about damages.

phrases.english: He said to him: I could answer you:
the first part is damages, and the last part is a fine;
phrases.notes: The 'fine' here is the thirty shekels paid when an ox kills a slave.

phrases.aramaic: מִיהוּ שִׁנּוּיָיא דְחִיקָא לָא מְשַׁנֵּינָא לָךְ.
phrases.english: but a forced answer I will not give you.
Both this and that are damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from the last part of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects a split reading of the משנה and keeps one consistent reading (damages in both parts), with an explanation still to come
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last part of the משנה must be about the קנס of a slave, so the whole משנה deals with fixed Torah payments, including כופר
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parts of the משנה refer to דמים. רבה's rule that כופר depends on the ox being stoned still stands, pending the explanation of the last part.
